title: V8 garbage collection: generations, mark-sweep, and compaction
hook: V8 splits the heap into young and old generations. Most objects die young — Scavenge copies survivors in milliseconds. Long-lived objects graduate to old space where Mark-Sweep-Compact runs less often but pauses longer.

blocks.text: **Generational hypothesis**: most allocations are short-lived. **Young generation** (nursery): new objects allocated in **From-Space**; **Scavenge** (minor GC) copies live objects to **To-Space**, discards dead. Survivors age; after threshold, **promoted** to **old generation**. **Old generation**: **Mark-Sweep** finds unreachable objects; **Mark-Compact** defragments. **Incremental/concurrent** marking reduces pause times in modern V8.

entries.plainDefinition: Move survivor from young to old gen.

blocks.text: GC pauses cause tail latency spikes in Node APIs. Allocating millions of short objects per request triggers frequent Scavenge — CPU spent on GC not business logic. Tuning `--max-old-space-size` and reducing allocation rate fixes production OOM.

blocks.title: GC is non-deterministic
blocks.body: You cannot force GC in production reliably — fix retention, not gc() calls.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Calling global.gc() in prod. Assuming GC runs immediately when reference nulled. Creating long-lived closures holding huge arrays.

blocks.text: Use --trace-gc in staging to correlate pauses with QPS. Orinoco is V8 GC project name. Major GC during Redis pipeline batch causes p99 spike — pool object reuse reduces promotion.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot name young vs old gen. Says reference counting is primary V8 strategy. Thinks delete obj frees memory instantly.

interviewTakeaways: Young gen Scavenge; old gen mark-sweep-compact.
Most objects die young — generational hypothesis.
Promotion = survivor moves to old space.
60s: Allocate nursery. Scavenge copies live. Promote survivors. Old gen mark-sweep. Pauses correlate with live set size. Fix retention not gc().
commonPitfalls: Weak: reference counting mental model — V8 is tracing.
Weak: unbounded Map as cache — old gen leak.
Strong: young/old + Scavenge vs mark-sweep + production metrics.
